::: {#sol-any-curve}

Yes,
with enough [unit](#def-unit)s.
Mark points on the graph of $f$ at closely spaced values of $z$,
and join neighbouring points with straight lines.
Because $f$ is continuous on a closed interval,
it changes little between nearby points,
so the joined-up graph stays as close to $f$ as you like
once the points are close enough together.
Call the inner points $t_1 < \dots < t_{n - 1}$,
and the slopes of the $n$ pieces $s_1, \dots, s_n$.
A network like the one in @exr-relu-bends draws the joined-up graph on $[a, b]$ with $n$ [unit](#def-unit)s,
one per piece,
each with $w_i = 1$:

- $c = f(a)$ starts the graph at the first point;
- the unit $s_1 \maxf{0, z - a}$ gives the first piece its slope;
- for each inner point $t_j$,
  the unit $\paren{s_{j + 1} - s_j} \maxf{0, z - t_j}$ is 0 to the left of $t_j$,
  and changes the slope from $s_j$ to $s_{j + 1}$ at $t_j$.

:::
